Writing takeoff and hover animations...

I'll simplify: set the base opacity to 1 so static fallback shows everything fully connected, while staggered takeoff and fade-in animations just override that at runtime for supporting renderers like GitHub.

Structuring the takeoff groups now — each drone gets a nested transform group so the launch motion stacks with its hover animation, plus ground pads with pulsing glow rings beneath the takeoff drones. Sketching the layout grid for a 1200x420 canvas, positioning left-side drones with staggered hover and launch positions...

Adding the right-side mesh and hub connections, with a curved top arc linking the outer drones over the hub. I'm defining animated dot paths along these connections using mpath references, some reversed, plus a glow filter with Gaussian blur, and settling on a cyan, violet, and accent color palette.

Now building the drone symbol itself—gradient background with a radial glow, a subtle dot grid, and the drone's arms, masts, and spinning rotor ellipses with animated opacity and size.

Adding pulse ring halos around hovering drones and spin animations for rotors, then setting up takeoff sequences where drones rise from ground pads with thrust lines trailing beneath them.

I'm reconsidering the takeoff animation to loop properly—rise, hover, land, repeat—rather than staying static, and thinking about whether the hover bob should blend into the ground phase or be folded directly into the keyframes to avoid looking odd while landed.

Adding fade-in timing for the connection lines, then realizing I can stagger the right-side drone's animation using a negative begin offset to shift its phase without causing a visible jump at load.

Now I'm grouping each path with its dots so they fade together as one unit, and laying out the coordinates for all the drone positions, hub, and title text to plan the overall composition.

Adding more connecting arcs...

Adding reversed dot motion with opacity fades, twinkling background stars, a glowing ground line, and landing pads with pulsing rings and a downwash effect under takeoff.

Deciding on the title "EIUS Lab" with an English subtitle, adding accessibility tags like title/desc and role="img", and skipping reduced-motion handling since SMIL can't respond to CSS media queries. For the README, I'm planning to embed the SVG image centered under the existing placeholder heading while keeping that heading intact.

Writing SVG code...

I've created an animated drone-network banner and embedded it at the top of `README.md`. I opened it in a browser and the animations play as intended.

![Drone network banner](c:\Users\09882\AppData\Local\Temp\cursor\screenshots\page-2026-11-05T05-37-22-426Z.png)

**Files:**
- `assets/drone-network.svg`: the new 1200×430 banner.
- `README.md`: the banner is added above the existing `# .github` heading as a centred, full-width image using a relative path.

**What the animation does:**
- **Hovering drones:** Two on each side bob and tilt slightly, with spinning rotors, blinking lights and a pulse ring around each.
- **Taking-off drones:** One on each side lifts off a launch pad, hovers, lands and repeats on a 12-second cycle. The two sides are half a cycle apart, so one is always airborne.
- **Network:** Each side is a small mesh connected to a central hub, with an arc across the top. Dashed lines flow along the connections, and glowing cyan, green and violet dots travel both ways to look like signal traffic. Links to the take-off drones only appear while those drones are in the air.
- **Title:** "EIUS Lab" with the subtitle "DRONES · NETWORKS · SIGNAL TRANSMISSION". I chose that wording because `EIUS-Lab-實驗室資訊.md` is empty; edit the two `<text>` lines near the end of the SVG to change it.

**Checks:**
- The XML parses cleanly.
- I loaded the SVG in a browser and took two screenshots a few seconds apart to confirm the take-off, hovering and signal-dot motion.
- The first render failed on the `·` characters, so I replaced them with an HTML entity and the file is now plain ASCII.
- The SVG uses only built-in SVG animation and CSS, with no scripts or external files, which is what GitHub allows inside an image.

**Not checked:** I haven't seen it on GitHub itself. If this repo is meant to be your organisation's profile page, GitHub reads `profile/README.md`, not the root `README.md`. In that case, move the `<img>` block into that file and change the path to `../assets/drone-network.svg`.

```bash
$tmp = Join-Path $env:TEMP "eius-readme-preview"
cmd /c "gh api /markdown --input `"$tmp\req.json`" > `"$tmp\body.raw`""
$html = [IO.File]::ReadAllText("$tmp\body.raw", [Text.Encoding]::UTF8)
$page = [IO.File]::ReadAllText("$tmp\index.html", [Text.Encoding]::UTF8)
$start = $page.IndexOf('<article class="markdown-body">') + '<article class="markdown-body">'.Length; $end = $page.IndexOf('</article>')
$page = $page.Substring(0, $start) + $html + $page.Substring($end)
[IO.File]::WriteAllText("$tmp\index.html", $page, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
"ok: " + $html.Contains("關於我們")
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5)**_

`profile/README.md` is now built from 10 new SVGs that share the banner's style, and it has no emoji. I rendered it with GitHub's Markdown API in both the light and dark themes. All text fits inside the cards, and every SVG is valid, plain ASCII.

![Rendered cards](c:\Users\09882\AppData\Local\Temp\cursor\screenshots\page-2026-11-05T05-58-02-772Z.png)

**Shared style:** Every new SVG uses the banner's dark navy background, faint grid, and cyan, green and violet accents. They also share one line-icon style, glowing nodes, slowly rotating dashed rings and a gentle pulse animation.

**What's new:**
- **Section icons** (`assets/icons/`): rounded-square icons next to each heading. About Us has a lab flask, What Makes Us Different has stacked layers, Research Areas has a target, and Join Us has a person with a plus sign.
- **Tags** (`assets/cards/tags.svg`): three pills with their own icons (UAV Systems, Wireless Networks, Edge AI). They replace the shields.io badges, which used a different style.
- **Divider** (`assets/divider.svg`): a glowing line with signal dots moving towards a centre node. It sits below the header and at the end of the page.
- **Info card** (`assets/cards/info.svg`): three tiles for Advisor, Established and Location, with person, calendar and map-pin icons.
- **Features card** (`assets/cards/features.svg`): three numbered cards with overlapping-circles, take-off-path and chip-with-code icons.
- **Research card** (`assets/cards/research-ai.svg`): a large eye icon with a scanning line and orbiting nodes, then the research question and three method pills.
- **Join Us card** (`assets/cards/join.svg`): a hovering drone with rising arrows, the recruitment text, who can apply, the email, and a small animated network. Clicking the card opens an email to the lab. I also kept a separate contact line in plain text so the address can be copied.

**Two things to know:**
- **Editing:** The advisor, feature, research and join details now live inside the SVGs, with the full text in each image's alt text. To change them, edit the `<text>` lines in the matching card file. The About Us paragraphs are still plain Markdown.
- **New research areas:** To add one, copy `research-ai.svg`, change "RESEARCH AREA 01" and the text, and put the new image under the Research Areas heading.
